newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Tuan Sing gets nod for Australian hotels.
newsitem.headline: Tuan Sing gets nod for Australian hotels.

text.p: Diversified Singapore property group Tuan Sing Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday it had won the approval of shareholders in Australia's Grand Hotel Group (GHG) to buy a 39 percent stake in the group.
It said in a statement the approval meant there was now no need for a takeover bid, required under Australian law if a party aquires 20 percent or more of a company.
Tuan Sing agreed to buy 39 percent of GHG for about Singapore $88.75 million (A$80.68 million) in January.
The acquisition will make Tuan Sing the largest shareholder in the hotel group, Tuesday's statement said.
GHG owns the Hyatt Centre Perth and 50 percent of the Grand Hyatt Melbourne.
Tuan Sing said the acquisition was part of its policy of building up a portfolio of prime properties in the region.
Tuan Sing's net earnings for the 1996 financial year ended December 31 rose 140 percent to $38.59 million.
